name: Binomial Queue
description: A mergeable priority queue composed of a collection of binomial trees. A binomial tree B_k has 2^k nodes and is formed by linking two B_(k-1) trees, making one root the child of the other. The queue maintains at most one binomial tree of each order, analogous to binary number representation. Merge operates like binary addition of tree lists, insert is a merge with a single-node queue, and extractMin finds the minimum root among all trees, removes that tree, and merges its children back into the queue.

pseudocode.text: for k ← 0 to max order do
combine trees of order k from q1, q2, carry
if one tree → place in result
if two trees → link into carry of order k+1
if three trees → place one, link other two as carry
find tree with minimum root among all binomial trees
childrenQueue ← reverse children of removed root
if t1.root > t2.root then swap t1, t2
make t2 a child of t1

testCases.name: Sequential inserts with tree linking
testCases.description: Inserting 4 elements causes binomial tree merges: two B_0 trees link into B_1, then two B_1 trees link into B_2, resulting in a single B_2 tree

testCases.name: Extract min with children reinserted
testCases.description: Extracting the minimum removes the root with the smallest key; its children are reversed and merged back into the queue

testCases.name: Many inserts then drain
testCases.description: Six inserts create a binomial queue with trees of varying orders; three extractions return elements in sorted order demonstrating priority queue behavior
